name: Retatrutide
lead: Retatrutide (development code LY3437943) is an investigational once-weekly injectable peptide from Eli Lilly that activates three receptors: glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucagon [1][15]. It is being studied for obesity, type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, knee osteoarthritis and fatty liver disease, and as of the sources reviewed it has no regulatory approval [1][9].

In a phase 2 obesity trial published in 2023, retatrutide produced large dose-related weight loss in adults without diabetes [3]. Phase 3 results published in 2026 reported mean weight reductions of 17.6, 23.7 and 25.0 percent at 4, 9 and 12 mg after 80 weeks, versus 3.9 percent for placebo, according to Wikipedia's summary of the TRIUMPH-1 trial [1][7]. Reported adverse effects are mainly gastrointestinal and dose-related, with some mild heart-rate increases [1].

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities, retatrutide is discussed as a more powerful fat-loss peptide than semaglutide or tirzepatide. Because it is unapproved, supplies outside trials are sold by research-chemical vendors whose products are not regulated, and Wikipedia reports that Lilly has filed lawsuits against black-market sellers [1][24].

paras: Retatrutide has no approved indication. Phase 3 programs known as TRIUMPH (obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, knee osteoarthritis) and TRANSCEND (type 2 diabetes) are testing it [9][6]. An expanded-access protocol for pre-approval use is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov [16].

Appearance-focused users, mainly in bodybuilding and peptide forums, use research-labelled retatrutide to reduce body fat, sometimes alongside testosterone, growth hormone and other compounds [22][25]. The drug has no known mechanism for targeting facial fat; changes to the face would follow total fat loss. No trial has studied facial appearance.

The phase 2 trial in adults with obesity (BMI 30 or higher) tested retatrutide against placebo and examined dose-response relationships for efficacy and safety [3]. A systematic review of randomized trials reported mean weight loss typically between 15 and 24 percent over 48 to 72 weeks, depending on dose and population [1][11]. The 2023 type 2 diabetes phase 2 trial was a placebo- and active-controlled study of glucose and weight outcomes [4]. A body-composition substudy in people with type 2 diabetes was published in 2025 [8]. In a phase 2a trial in fatty liver disease, retatrutide was assessed for liver fat reduction [5].

Phase 3 data have begun to appear. Wikipedia reports TRIUMPH-1 results from an 80-week trial of 2,339 adults with obesity without diabetes, including reductions in knee osteoarthritis pain and sleep apnea severity [1][7]. TRANSCEND-T2D-1 reported results in type 2 diabetes with inadequate glycemic control on diet and exercise [6].

The safety profile is still being established. Reported adverse effects are gastrointestinal, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation and abdominal discomfort, and they increase with dose; fatigue, headache and mild heart-rate increases have been less common [1]. Meta-analyses report relatively low discontinuation rates and infrequent serious adverse events in trials [1][11]. As with other incretin-based drugs, loss of lean mass accompanies weight loss and reviews discuss the role of resistance exercise [13]. Long-term outcomes are not yet established, and products obtained outside trials have unverified identity, purity and dose.

GLP-1 receptor activation reduces appetite and increases satiety, and GIP activity is thought to add to metabolic effects. The glucagon-receptor component is intended to increase energy expenditure and fat oxidation, and may reduce liver fat [1][10]. Reviews describe the idea of combining receptors as a way to achieve greater weight loss than single or dual agonists [14].

Retatrutide is a synthetic peptide made by solid-phase peptide synthesis and containing non-standard residues including 2-aminoisobutyric acid and a lipidated lysine side chain with a C20 diacid, which binds albumin and supports once-weekly dosing [1].

Retatrutide is not approved by any regulator. Wikipedia reports that several black-market sellers appeared before approval and that Lilly has brought lawsuits against them [1]. A community subreddit exists for discussion of the compound [17].

T Nation members report starting retatrutide for appetite control and fat loss, mention comparing it with tirzepatide and semaglutide, and list it in posts alongside anabolic compounds and growth hormone [19][21][22][23][24]. Some describe stronger fat loss than other GLP-1 drugs and others report less nausea [23][24]. Posters also ask where others sourced it, with one noting suspected underground-lab origin [24].

Retatrutide has phase 1 to phase 3 data. A phase 2 obesity trial, a phase 2 type 2 diabetes trial, a phase 2a fatty-liver trial and a body-composition substudy were published from 2023 to 2025 [3][4][5][8]. The TRIUMPH and TRANSCEND phase 3 programs are reporting from 2026 [7][6][9]. Meta-analyses summarize the early randomized data [11][12]. No published trial has tested retatrutide for facial appearance, and no human trial has tested research-labelled supplies.

timeline.event: Preclinical and early human description of LY3437943 as a triple agonist [15].
Phase 2 trials in obesity and type 2 diabetes published [3][4].
Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 and TRANSCEND-T2D-1 results published [7][6].

lore.intro: Retatrutide is discussed in peptide and bodybuilding forums as the strongest fat-loss option, usually obtained from non-clinical sources while it remains unapproved [17][24][22].

claims.claim: Retatrutide outperforms tirzepatide and semaglutide for fat loss.
claims.believers: T Nation posters say it is better for fat loss, with tirzepatide better for pure hunger control [21][24].
claims.experts: Published trials of retatrutide are placebo-controlled; no head-to-head trial against tirzepatide had been published in the sources reviewed [3].

claims.claim: Low-dose retatrutide gives fat loss with fewer side effects.
claims.believers: One forum member who switched from another GLP-1 drug says low-dose use reduced food noise without slight nausea [23].
claims.experts: Phase 2 data show gastrointestinal effects that increase with dose [1][3].

claims.claim: It can be run alongside TRT, anabolics and growth hormone for body recomposition.
claims.believers: Posters list retatrutide in stacks with testosterone, trenbolone and somatropin [22][25].
claims.experts: No published trial has tested these combinations; trials were of retatrutide alone against placebo [3][8].

claims.claim: Research-peptide vials are equivalent to the trial drug.
claims.believers: Users describe ordering vials from vendors and feeling effects soon after the first dose [19][24].
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports the existence of black-market sellers, and Lilly has sued some; no published study has verified purity or dose of such products [1].

claims.claim: Muscle can be kept while losing fat if protein and lifting are high.
claims.believers: Posters say they maintain high protein intake and lifting while on it [20][23].
claims.experts: A 2025 body-composition substudy and a narrative review discuss lean mass loss with incretin drugs and the role of resistance exercise [8][13].
